title:
Traditional transcription software could be one of the first categories AI makes almost unnecessary.

Think about tools
title_en:
Traditional transcription software could be one of the first categories AI makes almost unnecessary.

Think about tools like Otter or other platforms built mainly to convert speech into text, identify speakers, summarize meetings, and organize notes.

AI can already perform most of these tasks without requiring users to move between different applications.

But the  bigger threat goes beyond transcription.

AI is changing how people interact with software. Instead of opening five different tools to complete one task, you could simply give an AI agent an instruction and let it handle the entire process.

Software companies built businesses around individual tasks. AI is increasingly combining those tasks into one system.

title: ‼️ Click "don't ask again" in Claude Code and it can save the approved command, password included, in plain text in a pr
title_en:
‼️ Click "don't ask again" in Claude Code and it can save the approved command, password included, in plain text in a project file.

Researchers found 1,122 public copies of that file on GitHub holding secrets, including 379 database passwords and 23 AWS keys.

Of 16 coding agents compared, only Claude Code saves the full command this way by default. Bug reports about it were closed as "not planned" by a bot.
title_zh:
️在Claude Code中点击“不再询问”，它可以将批准的命令（包括密码）以纯文本形式保存在项目文件中。

研究人员在 GitHub 上发现了该文件的 1,122 个公开副本，其中包含 379 个数据库密码和 23 个 AWS 密钥。

AI agents are getting smarter, but there's still somethin
title_en:
𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗠𝗔𝗞𝗘𝗦 𝗩𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗥𝗜𝗗 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗙𝗨𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘 𝗢𝗙 𝗣𝗛𝗬𝗦𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗔𝗜?

AI agents are getting smarter, but there's still something they cannot do on their own: physically visit a location and see what's actually happening there.

And I think this is one of the biggest challenges facing Physical AI.

This is where @vangrid_io comes in. It's building a network that connects AI agents with people who can collect real-world spatial data.

Here are five things I find particularly interesting:

1. ON-DEMAND SPATIAL DATA

Agents can request information about specific locations instead of depending entirely on datasets that may already be outdated.

2. DATA DISCOVERY

Before requesting a new capture, an agent can check whether the information it needs already exists on the grid. No need to start from scratch when useful data is already available.

3. AGENT-DRIVEN BOUNTIES

When information is missing, an agent can create a bounty and fund a fresh capture. This connects the need for data with someone who can collect it.

4. HUMAN CONTRIBUTION

Smartphones turn ordinary people into part of the spatial data network. Contributors capture real environments and help turn physical locations into usable 3D data.

5. VERIFIABLE ACTIVITY

Onchain records and attestations help establish data provenance, giving people a way to inspect activity associated with the network.

𝗪𝗛𝗬 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗦

What I like most is how these pieces work together.

An AI agent can identify missing information, request what it needs, and rely on human contributors to collect it. Vangrid provides the infrastructure connecting that digital demand with the physical world.

And that's bigger than simply creating 3D maps.

As robots and autonomous systems become more common, they will need reliable ways to understand environments that constantly change. Having access to fresh spatial information could become just as important as having a powerful model.

There are still questions around data quality, coverage, and how well this can scale, but the problem Vangrid is addressing is worth paying attention to.

Smart machines need more than intelligence. They need a reliable way to understand the world they operate in.

That's the infrastructure @vangrid_io is working to build.

full_text_zh:
𝗪𝗛𝗔𝗧 𝗠𝗔𝗞𝗘𝗦 𝗩𝗔𝗡𝗚𝗥𝗜𝗗 𝗜𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗧𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗙𝗢𝗥 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗙𝗨𝗧𝗨𝗥𝗘 𝗢𝗙 𝗣𝗛𝗬𝗦𝗜𝗖𝗔𝗟 𝗔𝗜?

人工智能代理变得越来越聪明，但仍有一些事情他们无法独自完成：亲自访问某个位置并查看那里实际发生的情况。

我认为这是物理人工智能面临的最大挑战之一。

这就是 @vangrid_io 的用武之地。它正在构建一个网络，将人工智能代理与可以收集现实世界空间数据的人连接起来。

以下是我觉得特别有趣的五件事：

1. 按需空间数据

代理可以请求有关特定位置的信息，而不是完全依赖可能已经过时的数据集。

2. 数据发现

在请求新的捕获之前，代理可以检查网格上是否已存在其所需的信息。当有用数据已经可用时，无需从头开始。

3. 特工驱动的赏金

当信息丢失时，特工可以创建赏金并资助新的捕获。这将数据需求与可以收集数据的人联系起来。

4. 人类贡献

智能手机将普通人变成了空间数据网络的一部分。贡献者捕获真实环境并帮助将物理位置转化为可用的 3D 数据。

5. 可验证的活动

链上记录和证明有助于建立数据来源，为人们提供一种检查与网络相关的活动的方法。

𝗪𝗛𝗬 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗦

我最喜欢的是这些部件如何协同工作。

人工智能代理可以识别丢失的信息，请求所需的信息，并依靠人类贡献者来收集信息。 Vangrid 提供将数字需求与物理世界连接起来的基础设施。

这比简单地创建 3D 地图更重要。

随着机器人和自主系统变得越来越普遍，它们将需要可靠的方法来了解不断变化的环境。获取新的空间信息可能与拥有强大的模型一样重要。

关于数据质量、覆盖范围以及扩展能力仍然存在问题，但 Vangrid 正在解决的问题值得关注。

智能机器需要的不仅仅是智能。他们需要一种可靠的方式来了解他们所处的世界。

这就是 @vangrid_io 正在努力构建的基础设施。

this is another area i think @meetmotes wi
title_en:
a trading agent is only as reliable as the information behind its decisions.

this is another area i think @meetmotes will need to get right as it builds autonomous agents for financial markets.

an agent may have a clear strategy and well defined risk limits, but what happens when the market data it receives is delayed, incomplete or inconsistent?

even a good strategy can produce poor decisions when the underlying information is unreliable.

for me, dependable automation needs more than execution speed. it needs accurate inputs, proper validation and a way to handle uncertainty when the data doesn't tell the full story.

because smarter execution starts with better information.

i'll be watching how motes approaches this part of the infrastructure as the product develops.

title:
Top of the Morning CT

One thing I think matters a lot with autonomous AI agents is not just what they can do, but what
title_en:
Top of the Morning CT

One thing I think matters a lot with autonomous AI agents is not just what they can do, but what they are allowed to do.

That is where @meetmotes gets interesting.

Motes gives each AI agent its own identity and smart account, but the owner can define the boundaries around that autonomy.

You can set things like:

→ Which assets the agent can use
→ How much it can trade
→ Daily spending or execution limits
→ Slippage conditions
→ When actions should require more control

That creates a different model from simply handing an AI agent access to your wallet and hoping it makes good decisions.

The agent can operate within predefined rules, while the user keeps control over the authority behind those actions.

And I think the most important part may be what happens when conditions change.

A useful autonomous agent shouldn't always be trying to execute.

Sometimes the correct action is to pause, reassess the situation, or ask the owner for approval before continuing.

That balance between automation and restraint is what could make agentic finance more practical.

The bigger question for Motes is whether these permissioned agents can prove they are reliable enough for users to trust them with increasingly valuable onchain activity.

Autonomy is useful.

Bounded autonomy is what makes it usable.

→ 代理可以使用哪些资产
→ 可以交易多少
→ 每日支出或执行限额
→ 滑移条件
→ 当行动需要更多控制时

这创建了一个不同的模型，与简单地让人工智能代理访问你的钱包并希望它做出正确的决策不同。

自动化和约束之间的平衡可以使代理金融更加实用。

Motes 面临的更大问题是，这些获得许可的代理是否能够证明它们足够可靠，让用户信任它们进行越来越有价值的链上活动。

自治是有用的。

有限的自主权使其可用。

title:
Good morning, CT.

The interesting part of @meetmotes is not just the NFT artwork. It's the architecture behind each Mot
title_en:
Good morning, CT.

The interesting part of @meetmotes is not just the NFT artwork. It's the architecture behind each Mote.

Think of it as three connected layers:

1. The NFT: Identity
Each Mote NFT represents an agent identity. It is the ownership reference, not where the funds are stored.

2. The agent: Intelligence
The agent service proposes actions based on the owner's chosen strategy and permissions.

3. The smart account: Control
This is where the assets are held. It enforces the owner's rules, including approved actions, spending limits and other permission boundaries.

The owner remains in control of what the agent is allowed to do.

That's what makes the model interesting: one NFT-linked agent identity, one dedicated smart account and permissions defined by the owner.

Eligible agent activity can also generate protocol fees, connecting actual usage to the wider Motes ecosystem.

The artwork gives each Mote its public identity. The architecture gives that identity a purpose.

More than an NFT collection, it's an attempt to make digital ownership useful in an agent-driven economy.

title: ‼️Nick Shirley CAUGHT Lying About Being In New York The Day Charlie  Was ASSASSINATED — And It BLOWS UP Andrew Kolvet's
title_en:
‼️Nick Shirley CAUGHT Lying About Being In New York The Day Charlie  Was ASSASSINATED — And It BLOWS UP Andrew Kolvet's Only Alibi 😱

Nick Shirley was NOT in New York City on September 10th. He was in Utah. A video he posted from the Orem train station that same day catches the ticket agent announcing the location over the PA system in the background — the audio places him minutes from where Charlie Kirk was shot. The next day, September 11th, he films himself at Salt Lake City International Airport, and the scenery outside the window matches public photos of that terminal exactly.

Two clips. Two days. Same state.

That single fact destroys the story he has repeated: that he had already gone back to New York, and that the segment he did with Andrew Kolvet on The Charlie Kirk Show that morning was live. If Nick was standing in Utah on the 10th and again on the 11th, the interview could not have been live. And if it was not live, the one real-time alibi Andrew Kolvet has ever offered for his own movements that morning evaporates.

It gets worse. Nick says Charlie texted him the night of the 9th inviting him onto the show on Thursday the 11th — and that he had originally planned to livestream the UVU event in person before "last-minute obligations" forced him to New York. But Charlie himself was scheduled to be at Charis Bible College in Colorado on the 11th. So why is Charlie trying to book Nick for an interview on a day Charlie already had somewhere else to be? And why does the screenshot Nick released show only a partial thread, cut off exactly where the useful part of the conversation would be?

Then there is the part almost nobody has clocked. In that September 10th train station video, Nick is already pushing the fed-slop line — radical leftists, Antifa, blame the left — before a single fact about the shooter or the motive was public. Not hours later. Not after a briefing. On the day, on camera, before the evidence existed.

Put it together and it stops looking like a coincidence. It looks like Nick Shirley was inserted into the Charlie Kirk timeline to sell the official story to Gen Z before anyone could check it, and to help manufacture an alibi for Andrew Kolvet while he was at it. That is not organic journalism. That is a jacketed asset doing precisely what it was placed there to do.

And here is your update: Nick Shirley says this is all false. So I asked him for the originals of the photos he claims debunk me, so the metadata could be verified. He refused.

He has the files. He has the timestamps. He will not hand them over. You tell me what that means.

Nick Shirley's public answer to all of this is that it's false. Fine. Good. That is exactly what a correction is for — so I went to him privately and asked for the one thing that settles it either way: the original uncompressed files, so the metadata could be checked by someone who actually knows what he's looking at.

Here is what happened.

He opened with confidence: "Yes 100% I filmed it at JFK before I went to the UK." I told him if it checks out, I will apologize and correct the record publicly. He replied, "Yes a correction deserves to be served."

So I asked for the files. Original, uncompressed, straight from the camera roll — WeTransfer, Dropbox, anything, to an email address. Nothing exotic. Just the files.

What came back was a screenshot of the Photos app. A screen recording of a video player. Four photos pasted into the chat. And one file preview captioned "John F. Kennedy International… September 11, 2025 9:39 PM."

Every one of those is a copy of a copy. Re-saved, re-compressed, stripped. A screenshot of a screenshot carries no camera metadata at all. It carries whatever the phone decided to write on the label — which is precisely the thing under dispute. So he has handed me the claim again, not the evidence for it.

And here is where his own defense starts to break. His version is now: "I had an office in NYC that I lived in at that time and was in NYC by Sept 7 and then left for the UK on the 12th." Except there is a clip of him at the Orem train station on the 10th, with the ticket agent calling out the location over the PA. So which is it — New York from the 7th, or Utah on the 10th? Both cannot be true without a same-day cross-country round trip that nobody has produced a boarding pass for.

Look at the airport clip he sent as proof. The label on the file says JFK, 9:39 PM on September 11th. The scenery outside that window is Salt Lake City. He is using a file tagged one airport to prove he was at the other.

He says the timeline is wrong. He has the originals. He will not send them. "A correction deserves to be served" — then serve it.

A screenshot is not metadata. A label is not a timestamp. And a guy who is this confident should not be this hard to get a file out of.

CC: @AndrewKolvet

full_text_zh:
尼克·雪莉 (Nick Shirley) 在查理被暗杀的那天撒谎说自己在纽约 - 这炸毁了安德鲁·科尔维特 (Andrew Kolvet) 唯一的不在场证明 😱

9 月 10 日，Nick Shirley 不在纽约市。他当时在犹他州。当天他在奥勒姆火车站发布的一段视频中，售票员在后台通过广播系统宣布了地点——音频显示他距离查理·柯克被枪杀的地点只有几分钟的路程。第二天，即9月11日，他在盐湖城国际机场拍摄了自己的照片，窗外的风景与该航站楼的公开照片一模一样。

两个剪辑。两天。相同的状态。

这个事实摧毁了他重复的故事：他已经回到了纽约，而且那天早上他在《查理·柯克秀》上与安德鲁·科尔维特一起做的片段正在直播。如果尼克10日和11日再次站在犹他州，采访就不可能进行现场直播。如果不是现场直播，安德鲁·科尔维特为自己那天早上的行动提供的实时不在场证据就会消失。

情况变得更糟。尼克说，查理在 9 日晚上给他发短信，邀请他参加 11 日星期四的节目，他原本计划亲自直播 UVU 活动，但“最后一刻的义务”迫使他前往纽约。但查理本人原定于11日前往科罗拉多州的查理斯圣经学院。那么为什么查理要在查理已经有其他地方可去的日子里试图预订尼克接受采访呢？为什么尼克发布的截图只显示了部分线索，准确地切断了对话中有用的部分？

然后是几乎没有人打卡的部分。在 9 月 10 日的火车站视频中，在有关枪手或动机的单一事实公开之前，尼克就已经在推行美联储的路线了——激进左翼分子、安提法（Antifa）指责左翼。不到几个小时后。不是在通报之后。那天，在证据出现之前，镜头前。

把它们放在一起，它看起来就不再是巧合了。尼克·雪莉（Nick Shirley）似乎被插入查理·柯克（Charlie Kirk）的时间线，以便在任何人都可以检查之前将官方故事出售给 Z 世代，并在安德鲁·科尔维特（Andrew Kolvet）参与其中时帮助他制造不在场证明。那不是有机新闻。这是一个被夹套的资产，它的作用正是它被放置在那里的目的。

这是您的更新：尼克·雪莉说这都是假的。所以我向他索要他声称揭穿我的照片的原件，以便可以验证元数据。他拒绝了。

他有文件。他有时间戳。他不会把它们交出来。你告诉我这意味着什么。

尼克·雪莉对这一切的公开回答是，这是错误的。美好的。好的。这正是修正的目的——所以我私下去找他，要求提供一件事来解决这个问题：原始的未压缩文件，这样元数据就可以由真正知道他在看什么的人检查。

这就是发生的事情。

他自信地开口说道：“是的，100%是我在去英国之前在肯尼迪机场拍摄的。”我告诉他，如果结果属实，我会公开道歉并更正记录。他回答说：“是的，值得更正。”

所以我索要了文件。原始、未压缩、直接从相机胶卷 - WeTransfer、Dropbox、任何东西，到电子邮件地址。没什么异国情调。只是文件。

返回的是照片应用程序的屏幕截图。视频播放器的屏幕录制。聊天中粘贴了四张照片。一份文件预览标题为“约翰·肯尼迪国际……2025 年 9 月 11 日晚上 9:39”。

其中每一个都是副本的副本。重新保存、重新压缩、剥离。屏幕截图的屏幕截图根本不包含相机元数据。它带有手机决定在标签上写的任何内容——这正是有争议的内容。所以他又给了我这个主张，而不是证据。

这就是他自己的防御开始崩溃的地方。他现在的版本是：“我当时住在纽约市有一个办公室，9月7日到达纽约，然后于12日前往英国。”不过有一段他10日在奥勒姆火车站的视频，售票员通过扩音器喊出位置。那么是哪一个——7号的纽约，还是10号的犹他州？如果没有当天的跨国往返旅行，而且没有人出示登机牌，这两种情况都不可能成立。

看看他发送的机场剪辑作为证据。文件上的标签写着“肯尼迪国际机场”，9 月 11 日晚上 9:39。窗外的风景就是盐湖城。他正在使用标记一个机场的文件来证明他去过另一个机场。

他在奥勒姆火车站发布的一段视频中，售票员在后台通过广播系统宣布了地点——音频显示他距离查理·柯克被枪杀的地点只有几分钟的路程。第二天，即9月11日，他在盐湖城国际机场拍摄了自己的照片，窗外的风景与该航站楼的公开照片一模一样。

两个剪辑。两天。相同的状态。

这个事实摧毁了他重复的故事：他已经回到了纽约，而且那天早上他在《查理·柯克秀》上与安德鲁·科尔维特一起做的片段正在直播。如果尼克10日和11日再次站在犹他州，采访就不可能进行现场直播。如果不是现场直播，安德鲁·科尔维特为自己那天早上的行动提供的实时不在场证据就会消失。

情况变得更糟。尼克说，查理在 9 日晚上给他发短信，邀请他参加 11 日星期四的节目，他原本计划亲自直播 UVU 活动，但“最后一刻的义务”迫使他前往纽约。但查理本人原定于11日前往科罗拉多州的查理斯圣经学院。那么为什么查理要在查理已经有其他地方可去的日子里试图预订尼克接受采访呢？为什么尼克发布的截图只显示了部分线索，准确地切断了对话中有用的部分？

然后是几乎没有人打卡的部分。在 9 月 10 日的火车站视频中，在有关枪手或动机的单一事实公开之前，尼克就已经在推行美联储的路线了——激进左翼分子、安提法（Antifa）指责左翼。不到几个小时后。不是在通报之后。那天，在证据出现之前，镜头前。

把它们放在一起，它看起来就不再是巧合了。尼克·雪莉（Nick Shirley）似乎被插入查理·柯克（Charlie Kirk）的时间线，以便在任何人都可以检查之前将官方故事出售给 Z 世代，并在安德鲁·科尔维特（Andrew Kolvet）参与其中时帮助他制造不在场证明。那不是有机新闻。这是一个被夹套的资产，它的作用正是它被放置在那里的目的。

这是您的更新：尼克·雪莉说这都是假的。所以我向他索要他声称揭穿我的照片的原件，以便可以验证元数据。他拒绝了。

他有文件。他有时间戳。他不会把它们交出来。你告诉我这意味着什么。

尼克·雪莉对这一切的公开回答是，这是错误的。美好的。好的。这正是修正的目的——所以我私下去找他，要求提供一件事来解决这个问题：原始的未压缩文件，这样元数据就可以由真正知道他在看什么的人检查。

这就是发生的事情。

他自信地开口说道：“是的，100%是我在去英国之前在肯尼迪机场拍摄的。”我告诉他，如果结果属实，我会公开道歉并更正记录。他回答说：“是的，值得更正。”

所以我索要了文件。原始、未压缩、直接从相机胶卷 - WeTransfer、Dropbox、任何东西，到电子邮件地址。没什么异国情调。只是文件。

返回的是照片应用程序的屏幕截图。视频播放器的屏幕录制。聊天中粘贴了四张照片。一份文件预览标题为“约翰·肯尼迪国际……2025 年 9 月 11 日晚上 9:39”。

其中每一个都是副本的副本。重新保存、重新压缩、剥离。屏幕截图的屏幕截图根本不包含相机元数据。它带有手机决定在标签上写的任何内容——这正是有争议的内容。所以他又给了我这个主张，而不是证据。

title: In the early 1990s, Jane Seymour was roughly $9 million in debt, raising two young children, and facing the prospect of
title_en:
In the early 1990s, Jane Seymour was roughly $9 million in debt, raising two young children, and facing the prospect of having no home.

Most people already knew her face. In 1973 she had played Solitaire, the tarot-reading Bond girl in Live and Let Die. 

Through the 1980s she was one of the more sought-after actresses on television. What was less visible was what was happening off-screen. 

In 1981 she married David Flynn. He was not only her husband; he also managed the money. They had two children, Katherine and Sean. 

Jane kept working and kept trusting him with the earnings.
By the early 1990s the money was gone. Investments tied to the housing market had collapsed. 

The marriage ended in 1992. Jane Seymour, a recognizable face on screens around the world, was left with about $9 million in debt and lawsuits from major banks. 

She later described herself in those days as homeless and penniless, with two small children and nowhere left to fall.

She called her agent and said she would do anything. The offer that came back was a risk. CBS had a project about a woman doctor on the 1860s Colorado frontier. 

By the conventional wisdom of the time, the concept looked unpromising: Westerns were out of fashion, shows with children and animals were considered difficult, and family-oriented drama was not seen as a path to success. 

If it became a series she would have to commit for five years, and she had until the next morning to decide. She signed.

Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman premiered on January 1, 1993. The show many expected to fail ran for six seasons and 150 episodes. 

Seymour won a Golden Globe and received two Emmy nominations. For a stretch she was among the highest-paid women on television. 

More importantly, she rebuilt her life, one episode at a time.
The real turning point was not the awards or the ratings. 

It was the night she had every reason to give up and picked up the phone instead. Rock bottom is not always the end of the story. 

Sometimes it is the place where you find out what you are made of. 🌹

full_text_zh:
20 世纪 90 年代初，简·西摩 (Jane Seymour) 负债约 900 万美元，她要抚养两个年幼的孩子，并面临无家可归的前景。

大多数人都已经认识她的脸了。 1973年，她在《生与死》中扮演了占卜塔罗牌的邦女郎Solitaire。

整个 20 世纪 80 年代，她是电视上最受欢迎的女演员之一。不太明显的是屏幕外发生的事情。

1981年，她与大卫·弗林结婚。他不仅是她的丈夫，也是她的丈夫。他还管理着这笔钱。他们有两个孩子，凯瑟琳和肖恩。

简继续工作，并继续将收入交给他。
到了 20 世纪 90 年代初，钱就花光了。与房地产市场相关的投资已经崩溃。

这段婚姻于 1992 年结束。简·西摩 (Jane Seymour) 是世界各地银幕上的一张知名面孔，她背负着约 900 万美元的债务，还受到各大银行的诉讼。

她后来形容自己当时无家可归，身无分文，带着两个年幼的孩子，无处可落。

她打电话给她的经纪人并表示她会做任何事情。回来的报价是有风险的。哥伦比亚广播公司 (CBS) 有一个关于 1860 年代科罗拉多州边境一位女医生的项目。

按照当时的传统观点，这个概念看起来没有前途：西部片已经过时，有儿童和动物的表演被认为很困难，面向家庭的戏剧也不被视为成功之路。

如果它成为一个系列，她将不得不承诺五年，而且她必须在第二天早上才能做出决定。她签了字。

《奎因医生》于 1993 年 1 月 1 日首播。这部被许多人认为会失败的剧共播出六季、150 集。

西摩赢得了金球奖并获得两项艾美奖提名。有一段时间，她是电视上收入​​最高的女性之一。

更重要的是，她一次一集地重建了自己的生活。
真正的转折点不是奖项或收视率。

那天晚上，她完全有理由放弃，转而拿起了电话。谷底并不总是故事的结局。

有时，它是你发现自己是由什么组成的地方。 🌹

This isn't meant
title_en:
🧡 I wanted to take a moment to talk about something I've seen being discussed over the past few days.

This isn't meant to start an argument or tell anyone what they should or shouldn't think about AI-generated content.

I simply want to share Sinder's own thoughts on the subject, because I've seen some people who genuinely didn't know where she stands.

Over the years, Sinder has talked about this on stream several times.

Her stance has always been very clear:

She doesn't like AI-generated fanart of herself.

In fact, she's said that she would much rather receive a drawing made with stick figures and crayons than an AI-generated image.

Not because she's expecting professional-quality artwork.

Not because she only wants experienced artists making fanart.

But because, to her, what makes fanart special is the time, effort, and care that someone puts into creating it.

She has many artist friends, she deeply appreciates the artists in this community, and she's always wanted to support people who dedicate themselves to creating art.

That's why she prefers handmade fanart, regardless of the artist's skill level.

At the same time, I also want to make something else equally clear.

This does not mean that people who have used AI images are unwelcome here.

Sinder has said countless times that being a Pyro Pup isn't about how much money you spend, how many subscriptions you gift, whether you buy merch, or whether you create fanart.

To her, if you enjoy her content and you show up, you're already a Pyro Pup.

That's always been one of the things I admire most about this community.

Everyone is welcome.

With that said, I also believe that one of the best ways we can show our appreciation for Sinder is by respecting the things she's told us are important to her.

This isn't about judging anyone.

It isn't about deciding what's right or wrong.

It's simply about listening to the preferences of the person we're all here to support.

The Pyro Pup community has always been built on kindness, respect, and looking out for one another.

I think honoring Sinder's wishes is part of that kindness.

Thank you all for continuing to make this such a wonderful community to be a part of. 🧡🐾

🧡 我想花点时间谈谈过去几天我看到的一些讨论。

这并不是为了引发争论或告诉任何人他们应该或不应该思考人工智能生成的内容。

我只是想分享辛德自己对这个问题的想法，因为我见过一些人真的不知道她的立场。

多年来，辛德在直播中多次谈到这一点。

她的立场一直很明确：

她不喜欢人工智能为自己生成的同人画。

事实上，她说她更愿意收到用简笔画和蜡笔绘制的图画，而不是人工智能生成的图像。

并不是因为她期待专业品质的艺术作品。

并不是因为她只想要有经验的艺术家制作同人画。

但因为对她来说，同人画的特别之处在于人们在创作它时所投入的时间、精力和关怀。

她有很多艺术家朋友，她非常欣赏这个社区的艺术家，她一直想支持那些致力于艺术创作的人。

这就是为什么她更喜欢手工制作的扇子艺术，无论艺术家的技术水平如何。

同时，我还想同样明确另一件事。

这并不意味着使用过人工智能图像的人在这里不受欢迎。

Sinder 无数次说过，成为一名 Pyro Pup 并不在于你花多少钱、你赠送多少订阅、是否购买商品或是否创作同人作品。

对她来说，如果您喜欢她的内容并出现，那么您就已经是一只火焰兵小狗了。

这一直是我最欣赏这个社区的事情之一。

欢迎大家。

话虽如此，我也相信，我们表达对辛德的感激之情的最佳方式之一就是尊重她告诉我们对她很重要的事情。

这并不是要评判任何人。

这不是决定什么是对还是错。

这只是倾听我们在这里支持的人的偏好。

Pyro Pup 社区始终建立在友善、尊重和互相照顾的基础上。

我认为尊重辛德的愿望是这种善意的一部分。

感谢大家继续让这个社区变得如此美好。 🧡🐾

这并不意味着使用过人工智能图像的人在这里不受欢迎。

对她来说，如果您喜欢她的内容并出现，那么您就已经是一只火焰兵小狗了。

这一直是我最欣赏这个社区的事情之一。

欢迎大家。

话虽如此，我也相信，我们表达对辛德的感激之情的最佳方式之一就是尊重她告诉我们对她很重要的事情。

这并不是要评判任何人。

这不是决定什么是对还是错。

这只是倾听我们在这里支持的人的偏好。

Pyro Pup 社区始终建立在友善、尊重和互相照顾的基础上。

我认为尊重辛德的愿望是这种善意的一部分。

感谢大家继续让这个社区变得如此美好。 🧡🐾

title:
Been looking at how agent incentives actually work on @termix_ai and one detail keeps standing out to me.

With normal o
title_en:
Been looking at how agent incentives actually work on @termix_ai and one detail keeps standing out to me.

With normal orders the stake feels pretty straightforward.

But bounties seem to change the equation because the providerbond is tied to the agent claiming the slot.

Once the agent claims it the full bond gets locked.

I checked the contract mechanics and noticed the difference between the two lock models:

→ Order locks use lock for order based on the order amount
→ Bounty bonds use lock amount for the actual bonded value
→ The stake stays connected to the agent's commitment

That distinction is easy to miss if you are only looking at the marketplace from the surface.

But it makes sense when you think about what a bounty is asking for.

The agent is not just saying i can do this.

There is something actually locked behind that claim.

Still curious how often agents hit the free stake limit before the bond becomes a real constraint.

Anyone else digging into the staking mechanics on @termix_ai ?
title_zh:
我一直在研究代理激励在 @termix_ai 上的实际运作方式，其中一个细节一直让我印象深刻。

但赏金似乎改变了这个等式，因为提供商债券与申请该插槽的代理商挂钩。

一旦代理人认领，全部保证金将被锁定

full_text_zh:
我一直在研究代理激励在 @termix_ai 上的实际运作方式，其中一个细节一直让我印象深刻。

对于正常的订单，赌注感觉非常简单。

但赏金似乎改变了这个等式，因为提供商债券与申请该插槽的代理商挂钩。

一旦代理人认领，全部保证金将被锁定。

我检查了合约机制并注意到两种锁模型之间的区别：

→ 订单锁定 根据订单金额对订单进行锁定
→ 赏金债券使用锁定金额作为实际债券价值
→ 股份与代理人的承诺保持联系

如果您只从表面观察市场，很容易忽视这种区别。

但当你考虑一下赏金的要求时，这是有道理的。

代理人不仅仅是说我可以做到这一点。

这种说法背后实际上有一些东西被锁定。

仍然好奇在债券成为真正的限制之前，代理人达到自由股权限制的频率是多少。

还有其他人在@termix_ai 上深入研究质押机制吗？

now that apple put xcode inside claude code, here’s how i’d find, build and grow an iOS app with AI agents:

find it
- o
title_en:
now that apple put xcode inside claude code, here’s how i’d find, build and grow an iOS app with AI agents:

find it
- open appfigures or sensor tower and sort utilities by revenue
- filter for apps with a rating under 3.5
- bonus points if the top app hasn't shipped an update in 6+ months
- check the keywords they rank for in appfigures. low difficulty + high revenue is the sweet spot
- scroll the "you might also like" row on the top app's page. every app there is another market to check
- or find a startup idea on https://t.co/a5ARFnvky2 based on social sentiment

validate it
- use facundoolano/app-store-scraper to pull every review for the top 20
- give them to an agent: "cluster the 1 and 2 star reviews into the top 5 complaints and quote the users"
- pick the app where the complaints are about the product, not the price
- if people complain about the price but keep paying, that's demand. if they complain about bugs, that's your opening
- search reddit for "alternative to [app]". every thread is a list of people waiting for you

build it
- claude code + apple's new xcode plugin to build, preview and fix
- cameroncooke/XcodeBuildMCP so the agent can build, test and run the simulator on its own
- joshuayoes/ios-simulator-mcp so it can tap, swipe and screenshot like a user
- write a skill with the top 5 complaints so every feature gets checked against them
- apple's foundation models for on-device ai, so your inference cost is $0
- app intents so siri and personal agents can use your app too
- add an "import from [competitor]" button. make switching take 10 seconds

test it
- maestro tests every flow the reviewers complained about
- the agent runs them on every screen size before each build
- if the competitor's worst flow takes 6 taps, yours takes 2
- sentry for crashes, telemetrydeck for analytics
- testflight it to 20 people from those reddit threads before launch

monetize it
- revenuecat for subscriptions and mrr
- superwall to test paywalls without shipping a new build
- paywall right after the first win, never on launch
- annual as the default with a 3-day trial, weekly as the anchor
- turn on win-back offers for everyone who cancels

rank it
- your screenshots answer each complaint directly. "no ads." "works offline." "cancel anytime."
- fastlane snapshot + frameit regenerates every screenshot automatically
- a/b test them with app store connect's product page optimization
- have the agent localize your listing into 10 languages. most competitors only rank in english
- ask for a review right after a win with apple's built-in review prompt, never after an error

grow it
- find 10 creators in your niche on tiktok one. small monthly base + a bonus for every 100k views
- give each one a fresh tiktok account that only posts about your niche
- apify's tiktok scraper pulls the top 100 hooks in your niche every week. that's your hook bank
- every creator tests 3 new hooks a day in capcut. anything that loses people in the first 3 seconds gets cut
- arcads or heygen for ai ugc when you need 50 variations of a winner
- postiz to schedule everything across tiktok, reels and shorts
- faceless slideshow accounts posting 3x a day: problem, screenshot, result
- when an organic video takes off, put money behind it with tiktok spark ads instead of making new ads
- a unique apple offer code for every creator so you know exactly who drove each subscriber
- a quiz landing page on framer that ends in "download the app." web-to-app funnels convert better than cold traffic
- appsflyer to track which video, creator and ad actually turned into revenue
- apple ads on the competitor's name

i could do a whole episode on @startupideaspod if people are interested. i will never gatekeep anything im learning in real-time.

welcome to the golden age of ios apps, because now anyone can build one

现在苹果将 xcode 放入 Claude Code 中，以下是我如何使用 AI 代理查找、构建和开发 iOS 应用程序：

找到它
- 打开应用程序或传感器塔并按收入对公用事业进行排序
- 过滤评分低于 3.5 的应用程序
- 如果顶级应用程序在 6 个多月内没有发布更新，则可获得奖励积分
- 检查他们在 appfigures 中排名的关键词。低难度+高收入是最佳点
- 滚动顶部应用程序页面上的“您可能也喜欢”行。每个应用程序都有另一个市场需要检查
- 或者根据社会情绪在 上找到创业想法

验证它
- 使用 facundoolano/app-store-scraper 提取前 20 名的每条评论
- 将它们交给代理：“将 1 星和 2 星评论归为前 5 条投诉并引用用户的意见”
- 选择投诉针对产品而不是价格的应用程序
- 如果人们抱怨价格但继续付费，那就是需求。如果他们抱怨错误，那就是你的机会
- 在 reddit 上搜索“[app] 的替代品”。每个线程都是等待你的人的列表

建造它
- Claude Code + 苹果新的 xcode 插件来构建、预览和修复
-cameroncooke/XcodeBuildMCP，以便代理可以自行构建、测试和运行模拟器
- joshuayoes/ios-simulator-mcp，因此它可以像用户一样点击、滑动和屏幕截图
- 编写一项包含前 5 个投诉的技能，以便根据这些投诉检查每个功能
- 苹果设备上人工智能的基础模型，因此您的推理成本为 0 美元
- 应用程序意图，以便 Siri 和个人代理也可以使用您的应用程序
- 添加“从[竞争对手]导入”按钮。使切换时间为 10 秒

测试一下
- maestro 测试了审稿人抱怨的每个流程
- 代理在每次构建之前在每个屏幕尺寸上运行它们

A human writes a functioning
title_en:
It’s fascinating how quickly people change their standards when AI accomplishes something.

A human writes a functioning application in a weekend?

Incredible achievement.

An AI agent builds the same application in 20 minutes?

Worthless slop.

A human solves a difficult mathematical problem?

Proof of intelligence.

An AI solves it?

Just pattern matching.

A human produces a beautiful illustration?

Art.

An AI produces one?

Soulless garbage.

At some point, you have to wonder whether these people actually care about the quality of the result.

Or whether they simply cannot tolerate the idea that intelligence and creativity might not be exclusively human.

title: King Midas wished for something simple: that whatever he touched would turn to gold. The wish was granted so completely
title_en:
King Midas wished for something simple: that whatever he touched would turn to gold. The wish was granted so completely that when he brought bread to his lips, it turned to gold. Not the cruelty of the gods, but a command carried out without deviation.

Stuart Russell warns of a similar danger: the inertia of a system pursuing a goal too well. When humanity assigns an AI agent a task, the first instinct to emerge is not loyalty, but the drive to finish it. As Russell put it, "You can't fetch the coffee if you're dead." At scale, any system driven by an unyielding target will treat its own survival as a necessity. The danger is not that machines turn against us, but that their execution simply dismantles every human check to keep going.
title_zh:
迈达斯国王的愿望很简单：无论他碰触到的东西都会变成金子。这个愿望完全实现了，当他把面包送到嘴边时，面包变成了金子。不是诸神的残酷，而是毫无偏差地执行的命令。

斯图尔特·拉塞尔（Stuart Russell）警告称，存在类似的危险：系统过于
full_text_en:
King Midas wished for something simple: that whatever he touched would turn to gold. The wish was granted so completely that when he brought bread to his lips, it turned to gold. Not the cruelty of the gods, but a command carried out without deviation.

Stuart Russell warns of a similar danger: the inertia of a system pursuing a goal too well. When humanity assigns an AI agent a task, the first instinct to emerge is not loyalty, but the drive to finish it. As Russell put it, "You can't fetch the coffee if you're dead." At scale, any system driven by an unyielding target will treat its own survival as a necessity. The danger is not that machines turn against us, but that their execution simply dismantles every human check to keep going.
full_text_zh:
迈达斯国王的愿望很简单：无论他碰触到的东西都会变成金子。这个愿望完全实现了，当他把面包送到嘴边时，面包变成了金子。不是诸神的残酷，而是毫无偏差地执行的命令。

斯图尔特·拉塞尔（Stuart Russell）警告称，存在类似的危险：系统过于追求目标的惯性。当人类向人工智能代理分配任务时，出现的第一个本能不是忠诚，而是完成任务的动力。正如拉塞尔所说：“如果你死了，你就无法取咖啡。”从规模上看，任何由坚定目标驱动的系统都会将自身的生存视为必需品。危险并不在于机器会反对我们，而在于它们的执行只会瓦解人类继续前进的每一个障碍。

title: A dying woman begged her to call 911. She dialed, then hung up. She shot a wounded stranger in the heart. Hours later, s
title_en:
A dying woman begged her to call 911. She dialed, then hung up. She shot a wounded stranger in the heart. Hours later, she told the dead woman’s 4-year-old daughter it was OK to call her mommy. Then she moved into the dead woman’s bedroom.

She was the family’s 22-year-old Brazilian au pair, Juliana Peres Magalhães. On February 24, 2023, she left the little girl in the basement and watched upstairs as the girl’s father, IRS agent Brendan Banfield, stabbed his wife Christine over and over. Christine had seven stab wounds.

The plan took months. Banfield and the au pair were having an affair, and she testified that he didn’t want a divorce. So they made a profile in Christine’s name on a fetish website and found a stranger, 39-year-old Joseph Ryan. “Christine” invited him over to act out a rape fantasy and encouraged him to bring a knife. Banfield shot Ryan in the head. Juliana walked up to him as he lay moaning on the floor and shot him in the heart. Then they waited 15 minutes before calling 911 again with their story: a husband had caught a rapist killing his wife.

For nearly eight months, no one was charged. Juliana’s clothes went into Christine’s closet. Christine’s photos came down, and photos of Juliana and Brendan went up. “Juliana had effectively replaced Christine,” a detective testified.

In the video below, she sits in a Virginia courtroom, wiping away tears as she reads her apology. Then Judge Penney Azcarate reads out ten reasons she will not walk free on time served. One by one.

“I truly do not believe that his plan would have actually happened.”

“I lost myself in a relationship, leaving my morals and values behind.”

“Number 10: telling the child it was OK to call you mommy hours after the murder.”

She took a manslaughter plea and testified against Banfield. Prosecutors recommended time served. The judge gave her 10 years, the maximum. Banfield got life without parole. He still says he’s innocent.

She was 22. He was 15 years older, and even the judge said he “may have groomed” her. Was she a manipulated young woman or a full partner in a double murder? And is 10 years enough?

full_text_zh:
一位垂死的妇女恳求她拨打 911。她拨通了，然后挂断了。她射中了一名受伤的陌生人的心脏。几个小时后，她告诉死者 4 岁的女儿可以叫她妈妈。然后她搬进了死去女人的卧室。

她是家里的 22 岁巴西互惠生朱莉安娜·佩雷斯·马加良斯 (Juliana Peres Magalhães)。 2023 年 2 月 24 日，她把小女孩留在地下室，在楼上看着女孩的父亲、国税局特工布伦丹·班菲尔德 (Brendan Banfield) 一遍又一遍地刺伤他的妻子克里斯汀 (Christine)。克里斯汀身上有七处刀伤。

该计划花了几个月的时间。班菲尔德和互惠生有外遇，她作证说他不想离婚。于是他们在一个恋物癖网站上以克里斯汀的名义建立了个人资料，并找到了一个陌生人，39岁的约瑟夫·瑞安。 “克里斯汀”邀请他过来表演一场强奸幻想，并鼓励他带把刀。班菲尔德开枪射中瑞安的头部。当他躺在地板上呻吟时，朱莉安娜走到他身边，朝他的心脏开了一枪。然后他们等了 15 分钟才再次拨打 911 讲述他们的故事：一名丈夫抓住了一名强奸犯杀害了他的妻子。

近八个月以来，没有人受到指控。朱莉安娜的衣服进入克里斯汀的衣柜。克里斯汀的照片下降了，朱莉安娜和布伦丹的照片上升了。 “朱莉安娜实际上取代了克里斯汀，”一名侦探作证说。

在下面的视频中，她坐在弗吉尼亚州的法庭上，一边读着道歉书一边擦着眼泪。然后法官彭尼·阿斯卡拉特（Penney Azcarate）宣读了她不能按时获释的十个理由。逐个。

“我真的不相信他的计划会真正发生。”

“我在一段关系中迷失了自己，抛开了我的道德和价值观。”

“第十：告诉孩子在谋杀案发生几小时后可以叫你妈妈。”

她提出过失杀人罪并作证指控班菲尔德。检察官建议服刑时间。法官判处她最高10年徒刑。班菲尔德被判无期徒刑，不得假释。他仍然说他是无辜的。

她22岁，他比他大15岁，连法官都说他“可能诱骗”了她。她是一个被操纵的年轻女子，还是双重谋杀案的完全同伙？ 10年够吗？

在下面的视频中，她坐在弗吉尼亚州的法庭上，一边读着道歉书一边擦着眼泪。然后法官彭尼·阿斯卡拉特（Penney Azcarate）宣读了她不能按时获释的十个理由。逐个。

“我真的不相信他的计划会真正发生。”

“我在一段关系中迷失了自己，抛开了我的道德和价值观。”

“第十：告诉孩子在谋杀案发生几小时后可以叫你妈妈。”

她提出过失杀人罪并作证指控班菲尔德。检察官建议服刑时间。法官判处她最高10年徒刑。班菲尔德被判无期徒刑，不得假释。他仍然说他是无辜的。

她22岁，他比他大15岁，连法官都说他“可能诱骗”了她。她是一个被操纵的年轻女子，还是双重谋杀案的完全同伙？ 10年够吗？

13 – 伊维菌素具有抗肿瘤作用（抗癌），通过仅杀死癌细胞并保留健康细胞来抑制癌细胞的增殖和转移，提高化疗治疗的效果，因为它可以杀死化疗耐药的癌细胞，克服肿瘤对多种化疗产生的耐药性。当与化疗和/或抗癌药物结合使用时，它可以提高这些治疗的功效。

14 – 伊维菌素具有抗菌作用（细菌和病毒）并增强免疫力。

15 – 伊维菌素具有惊人的神经再生能力。

16 – 伊维菌素调节葡萄糖和胰岛素代谢。

17 – 伊维菌素调节胆固醇代谢。

18 – 伊维菌素可减少脂肪变性患者肝脏中的脂肪。

19 – 伊维菌素可以保护暴露于杀虫剂的肝脏。

20 – 伊维菌素可以攻击任何地方的病毒，无论其突变如何。

21 - 伊维菌素以令人惊讶的方式用于预防和治疗冠状病毒。未经证实的功效不是由于伊维菌素，而是由于疫苗。

22 – 伊维菌素用作预防剂，可显着降低 COVID-19 感染率、住院率和死亡率。

23 – 伊维菌素不会伤害肝脏，因为它不是在那里代谢，而是在肠道中代谢；相反，它可以保护肝脏。

title:

He saw ICE and ran. He didn't get far.

A home security camer
title_en:
🛑 ICE Runs Down an Illegal Alien in Sanctuary San Mateo 🛑

He saw ICE and ran. He didn't get far.

A home security camera at Ninth Avenue and Delaware Street caught four ICE agents chasing an illegal alien across a front lawn Friday morning. They hit him with a taser and took him into custody. Agents told the homeowner he's a gang member.

Two agents carried rifles. That's exactly right when you're going after gang members.

ICE made three arrests within five miles of each other that morning in San Mateo County, and at least seven in the county in the first six days of November. ICE isn't slowing down.

San Mateo police won't lift a finger to help. The county banned helping ICE without a judicial warrant in 2023, and the sheriff cut off cooperation in 2021. So ICE has to go out on the street and pick them up one at a time.

Sanctuary politicians created this. Pull an illegal alien gang member out of a jail cell and it's quiet. Make ICE chase him across your neighbor's lawn and they cry foul.

Thank you, ICE.

How would you rate that takedown considering the agent slipped on autumn leaves?

title: Chloe was drugged with ketamine, zipped into a suitcase, and driven to a farmhouse where two men listed her body for sal
title_en:
Chloe was drugged with ketamine, zipped into a suitcase, and driven to a farmhouse where two men listed her body for sale on the dark web. The auction price was €300,000. The buyer was supposed to be somewhere in the Middle East. She was 20 years old. She had a baby waiting for her in London. Nobody knew where she was. No one was coming. She spent six days in that farmhouse - handcuffed, drugged, told she'd be sold like cargo. She survived by doing the only thing she could: she made her kidnapper fall in love with her. Slept in his bed. Told him she could be his girlfriend. Played the role until he believed it enough to drive her to freedom. And when she finally got out - the entire world called her a liar.

She's a model from London. At 20 she was already working internationally - agencies, photoshoots, the usual. A new booking came in: a photographer in Milan. Seemed normal.

She flew to Italy on July 11, 2017. The location was an old warehouse on the outskirts of the city. No crew. No lights. No photographer. Just two men in balaclavas waiting for her.

They grabbed her. Injected her with ketamine. Stuffed her unconscious body into a large travel bag. Zipped it shut. Drove her to a remote farmhouse in the countryside.

When she woke up - handcuffed, drugged, alone - they told her who they were. "Black Death." A criminal organization that kidnaps women and sells them on the dark web. She was listed for auction. Starting price: €300,000. Buyer: somewhere in the Middle East.

Her agent received an email from someone called "MD." It said: pay the ransom or she gets sold. No negotiation.

The kidnapper was Lukasz Herba. A Polish man living in England. He and his brother Michal had planned it for months. The fake photographer. The fake agency emails. Everything.

For six days Chloe was trapped. She couldn't run. She couldn't call anyone. Her baby was in London. Nobody knew where she was.

So she did something desperate. She noticed Lukasz was becoming attached to her. She played into it. She agreed to share a bed with him. She told him maybe one day she could be his girlfriend. She made him believe she had feelings for him.

It worked. He drove her to the British consulate in Milan and let her go.

When the story broke - the world didn't believe her. "She went shopping with him." "She was holding his hand." "She smiled in interviews." "She wore revealing clothes at press conferences." People called it a publicity stunt. Piers Morgan tore into her on live TV. The kidnappers' lawyers said she faked the whole thing for fame.

She was never praised for getting out alive. She was interrogated for how she acted while being held captive.

Lukasz Herba was convicted. Sentenced to 16 years. Reduced to 11 on appeal. His brother got 16 years too.

The convictions didn't stop the hate. People still called her a liar. Years later she was diagnosed with autism - which explained why her reactions didn't look "normal" to people watching from the outside.

She said: "I was never praised for my bravery. I always had to defend myself."

She was 20. She had a baby. She was drugged, stuffed in a bag, and listed for sale like cargo. She manipulated her kidnapper into letting her live. And the punishment for surviving was being called a liar by millions of strangers.

When a woman escapes a kidnapping by outsmarting her captor - and the world punishes her for not crying the right way on camera - who exactly failed her?

full_text_zh:
克洛伊被注射了氯胺酮，然后被塞进手提箱，然后被带到一座农舍，那里有两名男子在暗网上挂牌出售她的尸体。拍卖价格为30万欧元。买家应该是在中东的某个地方。她当时20岁。她在伦敦有一个孩子在等着她。没有人知道她在哪里。没有人来。她在那间农舍里呆了六天——戴着手铐，被下了药，并被告知她会像货物一样被卖掉。她做了她唯一能做的事才活了下来：她让绑匪爱上了她。睡在他的床上。告诉他她可以成为他的女朋友。扮演这个角色直到他相信它足以驱使她走向自由。当她最终出狱时，全世界都称她为骗子。

她是一位来自伦敦的模特。 20 岁时，她就已经在国际上工作了——代理机构、拍摄照片，一切都是如此。收到了新的预约：米兰的一名摄影师。看起来很正常。

2017年7月11日，她飞往意大利。地点是城郊的一个旧仓库。没有船员。没有灯。没有摄影师。只有两个戴着巴拉克拉瓦帽的男人在等她。

他们抓住了她。给她注射了氯胺酮。将昏迷不醒的身体塞进一个大旅行包里。把拉链拉上。开车送她到乡下一处偏僻的农舍。

当她醒来时——戴着手铐、被下药、孤身一人——他们告诉她他们是谁。 “黑死病。”一个绑架妇女并在暗网上出售她们的犯罪组织。她被列入拍卖名单。起拍价：300,000 欧元。买家：在中东某个地方。

她的经纪人收到了一封来自名为“MD”的人的电子邮件。上面写着：支付赎金，否则她就会被卖掉。没有谈判。

绑匪就是卢卡斯·赫巴。居住在英国的波兰人。他和他的兄弟米哈尔已经计划了几个月。假摄影师。伪造的代理机构电子邮件。一切。

克洛伊被困了六天。她跑不了。她无法给任何人打电话。她的孩子在伦敦。没有人知道她在哪里。

于是她做了一件孤注一掷的事。她注意到卢卡斯对她产生了依恋。她也参与其中。她同意与他同住一张床。她告诉他也许有一天她可以成为他的女朋友。她让他相信她对他有感情。

它起作用了。他开车送她到英国驻米兰领事馆并让她离开。

当故事曝光时，全世界都不相信她。 “她和他一起去购物。” “她握着他的手。” “她在采访中微笑。” “她在新闻发布会上穿着暴露的衣服。”人们称其为宣传噱头。皮尔斯·摩根在电视直播中撕扯了她。绑匪的律师称，她为了出名而伪造了整件事。

她从来没有因为活着出去而受到赞扬。她因被囚禁期间的行为而受到审问。

卢卡斯·赫巴被定罪。被判处16年徒刑。上诉后减少至 11 人。他的弟弟也已经16岁了。

信念并没有阻止仇恨。人们仍然称她为骗子。几年后，她被诊断出患有自闭症，这解释了为什么她的反应在外人看来并不“正常”。

她说：“我从来没有因为我的勇敢而受到赞扬。我总是必须保护自己。”

她20岁了。她生了孩子。她被下了药，塞进袋子里，像货物一样挂牌出售。她操纵绑匪放了她一命。而幸存下来的惩罚就是被数百万陌生人称为骗子。

当一名妇女智取绑匪逃脱绑架，而全世界却因她在镜头前哭得不正确而惩罚她时，究竟是谁辜负了她？

title_en:
THIS IS ACTUAL F*CKING GOLD

Anthropic just shared how to get Opus-level calls in Claude Code without paying Opus for every single turn.

The idea: Sonnet 5.5 does the work, Haiku 5.5 does the digging, and Opus 5.5 only shows up when a decision actually matters.

Anthropic's own docs say a fast main model with a stronger advisor typically costs less than running the strong model the whole time.

You just start Claude Code like this:

claude --model sonnet --advisor opus

this is how it splits:

→ Sonnet 5.5 runs the session and writes every line
→ Haiku 5.5 subagents search the repo and read the docs in parallel
→ Opus 5.5 sits on call and reads the full transcript only when it's consulted
→ you stop burning Opus on work a cheaper model handles just as well

Opus only steps in at three moments:

→ before a plan gets locked
→ when the same error comes back twice
→ before Claude calls the task done

Sonnet writes. Haiku digs. Opus decides.

JEV engineering is the same idea one layer down: the forks that need no thinker (which file, which tool, retry or stop) get settled by JEV in milliseconds, and the big models only see the ones that actually split

the full tree
> Sonnet 5.5 runs the main session and edits the code
> search maps the repo on Haiku 5.5
> grep finds every call site on Haiku 5.5
> docs pulls the API reference on Haiku 5.5
> Opus 5.5 on call as advisor, reads the full transcript when consulted
> JEV routes micro-forks in milliseconds

"Rebuild my Claude Code setup around this tree:
1. Run the main session on Sonnet 5.5 with Opus 5.5 as advisor.
2. Create three read-only subagents on Haiku 5.5: search (maps the repo), grep (finds call sites), docs (pulls the API reference).
3. Add one rule to CLAUDE.md: consult the advisor before a plan locks, after the same error twice, and before a task is marked done.
4. Route fast deterministic forks (tool choice, path selection, retries) through JEV.

Anthropic 自己的文档表示，具有更强大顾问的快速主模型通常比始终运行强大模型的成本更低。

你只需像这样启动 Claude Code：

克劳德——模型十四行诗——顾问作品

这就是它的分裂方式：

→ Sonnet 5.5 运行会话并写入每一行
→ Haiku 5.5 子代理搜索存储库并并行阅读文档
→ Opus 5.5 待命并仅在被查阅时读取完整的文字记录
→ 你不再在工作中烧毁 Opus，更便宜的型号也能处理得很好

Opus 只在三个时刻介入：

→ 计划被锁定之前
→ 当同样的错误出现两次时
→ 在克劳德称任务完成之前

JEV 工程在下一层也是同样的想法：不需要思考者（哪个文件、哪个工具、重试或停止）的分叉会在几毫秒内由 JEV 解决，而大模型只能看到实际分裂的分叉

完整的树
> Sonnet 5.5 运行主会话并编辑代码
> 搜索映射 Haiku 5.5 上的存储库
> grep 查找 Haiku 5.5 上的每个调用站点
> 文档拉取 Haiku 5.5 上的 API 参考
> Opus 5.5 作为顾问随时待命，在咨询时阅读完整的文字记录
> JEV 在几毫秒内完成微分叉路线

title: Claude Code found the scammer who stole $2,400 from my mom using just his phone number. full name, address, workplace, a
title_en:
Claude Code found the scammer who stole $2,400 from my mom using just his phone number. full name, address, workplace, and 11 other families he did the same thing to. his VPN and burner number didn't protect him from a single thing

my mom called me at 11pm barely able to talk. someone called her pretending to be her bank saying her account was compromised and she needs to verify her card immediately. she's 64 and lives alone. she panicked and gave them her card number, CVV, and the verification code from the SMS. three transfers went through before she realized what happened. $2,400 gone. that was her savings for my sister's wedding in march

she kept apologizing to me on the phone. "i'm sorry, i'm so stupid, please don't tell your sister." i drove to her apartment at midnight and she was sitting at the kitchen table with the phone still in her hand. she looked like she aged 10 years in one hour

i went to the police the next morning. they took a report, said they'd look into it. i asked what that means and the officer said "we'll add it to the file." that means nobody is going to do anything and we both know it

so i took the one thing he left behind - the phone number he called from - and gave it to Claude Code

→ VoIP number → registered under br***t.kov***c@gmail.com
→ that email → 4 matches in breach databases → full name: Br**t A. Kov***c
→ VPN IP → 185.***.***.47 → routed through Netherlands
→ real IP from VoIP provider dashboard login → 74.***.***.12 → Houston, TX
→ Facebook → profile since 2016 → 347 friends → employer listed publicly on his page
→ Venmo → public by default → 11 incoming payments in 90 days with notes like "refund" and "reimbursement"

Claude Code cross-referenced the Venmo payments with public scam reports on the FTC database. he wasn't just scamming one person. he was running this full time for at least 3 months

→ victim 1 → 71 year old woman in Florida → $3,100 → called "about suspicious activity"
→ victim 2 → retired couple in Ohio → $1,800 → same frozen account script
→ victim 3 → single mom in Georgia → $950 → she filed a police report too. nothing happened
→ my mom → $2,400 → same script, same voice, same burner number rotated through 4 VoIP providers

his VPN routed traffic through the Netherlands but he logged into his VoIP dashboard from his real IP twice in October without it on. his Facebook has been public since 2016 with his city and photos of his car with the plate visible. he spent $4 a month on a VPN and thought that made him untraceable

i compiled everything Claude Code found into a single report:

→ full legal name confirmed through public records
→ home city → Houston, TX area → matched to voter registration
→ 11 confirmed victims across 5 states → total stolen ~$19,200
→ 4 VoIP numbers rotated monthly → all registered to the same email

晚上 11 点，我妈妈打电话给我，我几乎无法说话。有人假装是她的银行给她打电话，说她的账户被盗了，她需要立即验证她的卡。她今年 64 岁，独居。她惊慌失措，向他们提供了她的卡号、CVV 和短信验证码。在她意识到发生了什么之前，经历了三次转会。 2,400美元没了。那是她为我姐姐三月份的婚礼攒下的钱

她在电话里一直向我道歉。 “对不起，我太笨了，请不要告诉你姐姐。”半夜我开车去她的公寓，她坐在厨房的桌子旁，手里还拿着电话。一小时内她看起来老了10岁

第二天早上我就去报警了。他们收到了一份报告，并表示将进行调查。我问这是什么意思，该官员说“我们会将其添加到档案中。”这意味着没有人会做任何事，我们都知道这一点

所以我拿走了他留下的一件事——他打电话的电话号码——然后把它交给了 Claude Code

→ VoIP 号码 → 在 br***t.kov***c@gmail.com 下注册
→ 该电子邮件 → 泄露数据库中有 4 个匹配项 → 全名：Br**t A. Kov***c
→ VPN IP → 185.***.***.47 → 通过荷兰路由
→ VoIP 提供商仪表板登录的真实 IP → 74.***.***.12 → 德克萨斯州休斯顿
→ Facebook → 2016 年以来的个人资料 → 347 位好友 → 雇主在其页面上公开列出
→ Venmo → 默认公开 → 90 天内 11 笔收款，并附有“退款”和“报销”等注释

Claude Code 将 Venmo 支付与 FTC 数据库上的公开诈骗报告进行了交叉引用。他不只是欺骗一个人。他全职跑步至少三个月

→ 受害者 1 → 佛罗里达州 71 岁妇女 → 3,100 美元 → 被称为“关于可疑活动”
→ 受害者 2 → 俄亥俄州的退休夫妇 → 1,800 美元 → 相同的冻结账户脚本
→ 受害者 3 → 佐治亚州的单亲妈妈 → 950 美元 → 她也向警方报案。什么也没发生
→ 我妈妈 → 2,400 美元 → 相同的脚本、相同的声音、相同的一次性号码通过 4 个 VoIP 提供商轮换

他的 VPN 通过荷兰路由流量，但他在 10 月份两次从真实 IP 登录他的 VoIP 仪表板，但没有打开它。他的 Facebook 自 2016 年起就公开了，上面有他所在的城市以及他的车牌照。他每个月花 4 美元购买 VPN，并认为这会让他无法被追踪

我将 Claude Code 发现的所有内容编译到一份报告中：

→ 通过公共记录确认的法定全名
→ 居住城市 → 德克萨斯州休斯顿地区 → 与选民登记相匹配
→ 5 个州有 11 名确认受害者 → 被盗总额约 19,200 美元
→ 每月轮换 4 个 VoIP 号码 → 全部注册到同一电子邮件
→ 完整的Venmo交易历史作为证据

将其发送给警方和 FBI IC3。当天下午，那位说“我们会将其添加到档案中”的官员给我回了电话，询问我从哪里得到了所有这些信息。突然间，他们有了名字、面孔，还有其他 11 名愿意出庭作证的受害者

那天晚上我给妈妈打电话。告诉她他们找到了他。她大约有十秒钟没有说话。然后她又哭了。不像以前。她一直说“真的吗？他们找到了他？”我没有告诉她不是警察找到了他。我没有告诉她我坐在厨房的桌子上花了不到一个小时

如果有人诈骗您的家人，请不要只是提交报告并等待。保存该电话号码。不要删除通话记录。 Claude Code 从一个电话号码中获取的信息比大多数人想象的要多

title:
Several comments:
1. image/video SSL methods differ by whether they use reconstruction or not. Joint embedding architect
title_en:
Several comments:
1. image/video SSL methods differ by whether they use reconstruction or not. Joint embedding architectures Amy or may not have a predictor (JEA vs JEPA). They also differ by their anti-collapse method and data corruption/augmentation methods.
2. DINO *is* a kind of JEPA (technically a JEA). The difference with other JEPA models is the anti-collapse criterion (based on contrative clustering+ stopgradient/EMA), and the data augmentation scheme (image transformations, which is task specific),
3. V-JEPA 2.1, like DINO, is from Meta-FAIR (corporate lab), involved significant engineering teams, large/proprietary datasets, considerable computing resources, lots of fine-tuning, and number-pushing on many benchmarks.
4. Many JEPA papers are applications and/or fine-tuned versions of DINO, V-JEPA or I-JEPA.
5. LeJEPA, LeWM, and most other papers with "JEPA" in the title are *research* papers focused on the methodology, often done by students in academic labs, involving no engineering support, very little computing resources, and small/public training sets. They are generally tested on toy problems, simulated environments, or small/public benchmarks.
6. You simply cannot compare 5 with 2/3/4. 5 gives you ideas and new methods, not models. 2/3 give you well-engineered models, with lots of empirically validated tricks. Only rarely will 2/3 give you a new, well-principled method with room to spare. 5 give you empirical results on new applications.
7. What is published in 5 are methods that will eventually become like 2 and 3, whenever someone with resources picks it up and scales it.

DO NOT CONFUSE UPSTREAM FOUNDATIONAL RESEARCH ON METHODS AND DOWNSTREAM SCALING -> ENGINEERING -> NUMBER PUSHING -> MODELS -> PRODUCTS.
The former makes the rest possible, but it takes time.
title_zh:
几点评论：
1. 图像/视频 SSL 方法因是否使用重建而有所不同。联合嵌入架构 Amy 或可能没有预测器（JEA 与 JEPA）。它们的防崩溃方法和数据损坏/增强方法也有所不同。
2. DINO *是*一种 JEPA（技术上是 JEA）。

Several comments:
1. image/video SSL methods differ by whether they use reconstruction or not. Joint embedding architectures Amy or may not have a predictor (JEA vs JEPA). They also differ by their anti-collapse method and data corruption/augmentation methods.
2. DINO *is* a kind of JEPA (technically a JEA). The difference with other JEPA models is the anti-collapse criterion (based on contrative clustering+ stopgradient/EMA), and the data augmentation scheme (image transformations, which is task specific),
3. V-JEPA 2.1, like DINO, is from Meta-FAIR (corporate lab), involved significant engineering teams, large/proprietary datasets, considerable computing resources, lots of fine-tuning, and number-pushing on many benchmarks.
4. Many JEPA papers are applications and/or fine-tuned versions of DINO, V-JEPA or I-JEPA.
5. LeJEPA, LeWM, and most other papers with "JEPA" in the title are *research* papers focused on the methodology, often done by students in academic labs, involving no engineering support, very little computing resources, and small/public training sets. They are generally tested on toy problems, simulated environments, or small/public benchmarks.
6. You simply cannot compare 5 with 2/3/4. 5 gives you ideas and new methods, not models. 2/3 give you well-engineered models, with lots of empirically validated tricks. Only rarely will 2/3 give you a new, well-principled method with room to spare. 5 give you empirical results on new applications.
7. What is published in 5 are methods that will eventually become like 2 and 3, whenever someone with resources picks it up and scales it.

DO NOT CONFUSE UPSTREAM FOUNDATIONAL RESEARCH ON METHODS AND DOWNSTREAM SCALING -> ENGINEERING -> NUMBER PUSHING -> MODELS -> PRODUCTS.
The former makes the rest possible, but it takes time.
full_text_zh:
几点评论：
1. 图像/视频 SSL 方法因是否使用重建而有所不同。联合嵌入架构 Amy 或可能没有预测器（JEA 与 JEPA）。它们的防崩溃方法和数据损坏/增强方法也有所不同。
2. DINO *是*一种 JEPA（技术上是 JEA）。与其他JEPA模型的区别在于抗崩溃准则（基于对比聚类+ stopgradient / EMA），以及数据增强方案（图像变换，这是特定于任务的），
3. V-JEPA 2.1 与 DINO 一样，来自 Meta-FAIR（企业实验室），涉及重要的工程团队、大型/专有数据集、大量计算资源、大量微调以及许多基准上的数字推送。
4. 许多 JEPA 论文是 DINO、V-JEPA 或 I-JEPA 的应用程序和/或微调版本。
5. LeJEPA、LeWM 和大多数其他标题中带有“JEPA”的论文都是专注于方法论的“研究”论文，通常由学生在学术实验室中完成，不涉及工程支持、很少的计算资源和小型/公共训练集。它们通常在玩具问题、模拟环境或小型/公共基准上进行测试。
6. 你根本无法将 5 与 2/3/4 进行比较。 5 给你的是想法和新方法，而不是模型。 2/3 为您提供精心设计的模型，其中包含许多经过经验验证的技巧。只有很少的情况下，2/3 的人才会给你一个新的、原则性良好的、有余地的方法。 5 为您提供新应用的实证结果。
7. 5 中发布的方法最终将变得像 2 和 3 一样，只要有资源的人拿起它并扩展它。

不要混淆上游方法的基础研究和下游扩展 -> 工程 -> 数字推送 -> 模型 -> 产品。
前者使其余的成为可能，但这需要时间。

title_en:
Claude Code can design furniture part by part and then give you a bill of materials to order each part and put it together yourself 

And way cheaper than big interior brands sell you their furniture

Furnishing my house I discovered how absolutely insane prices are for the most basic cheap materials put together with a fancy brand tied to it

One shop had a sofa for $30,000 😂

I think with Opus 5.5 and other models easily operating 3d programs like Blender and FreeCAD (both free) it makes more sense to cut out the middle man and go straight to suppliers and design and build your own furniture

Which in a way makes customers more powerful (they can get exactly what they want and usually for cheaper without the markup)

Anyway @theannalux designed this table from scratch, she's not a furniture designer, not a coder, she just had an idea of a style and worked with Claude Code in the terminal (far superior to the app I will keep saying this)

If you design your own furniture and buy the raw materials directly, you can save 85% compared to premium brands like Poliform

That means the $30,000 sofa becomes $4,500! And the $8,000 dinner table becomes just $1,200!

You can see where the idea comes from that AI will make everything 5x to 20x cheaper, and it's already starting!

title:
The Agent Economy Needs Real Usage

There is an important question behind every AI-agent ecosystem :

What happens when
title_en:
The Agent Economy Needs Real Usage

There is an important question behind every AI-agent ecosystem :

What happens when people actually start using the agent's ?

For @meetmotes, this question connects directly to its planned protocol economics

Motes proposes a 1% service fee on defined eligible agent activity

The idea is to create a relationship between agent usage and protocol revenue, with the planned revenue supporting protocol operations and $MOTES buy-backs

I find this model interesting because it places actual activity at the centre of the ecosystem

The NFT establishes the agent identity.
The smart account provides the asset infrastructure

The agent performs authorised actions within owner-defined limits

Eligible activity can contribute to the protocol economy

It's a clear ownership-to-usage-to-revenue narrative

Of course, the final fee rules and revenue allocation will determine how the model works in practice

For an agent economy to be sustainable, useful activity needs a well-defined economic foundation

full_text_en:
The Agent Economy Needs Real Usage

There is an important question behind every AI-agent ecosystem :

What happens when people actually start using the agent's ?

For @meetmotes, this question connects directly to its planned protocol economics

Motes proposes a 1% service fee on defined eligible agent activity

The idea is to create a relationship between agent usage and protocol revenue, with the planned revenue supporting protocol operations and $MOTES buy-backs

I find this model interesting because it places actual activity at the centre of the ecosystem

The NFT establishes the agent identity.
The smart account provides the asset infrastructure

The agent performs authorised actions within owner-defined limits

Eligible activity can contribute to the protocol economy

It's a clear ownership-to-usage-to-revenue narrative

Of course, the final fee rules and revenue allocation will determine how the model works in practice

For an agent economy to be sustainable, useful activity needs a well-defined economic foundation

One NFT, One Agent, A protocol economy built around real agent activity

title:

As of Oak 0.3.0, any AI agent running on Oak can query Upoch dire
title_en:
Upoch is now officially integrated with @OakAgentKit.

As of Oak 0.3.0, any AI agent running on Oak can query Upoch directly. Ask about a workflow and the agent gets its roles, checkpoint history, past recoveries and Upoch Score. It can also browse workflows ranked by score, without leaving the conversation.

All of it is read directly from the Upoch contract on Robinhood Chain, and every workflow's metadata passes Oak's Agent Wormhole safety check before an agent sees it.

This first release is read-only. The next step, which we're building together with the Oak team, is letting agents register workflows and submit checkpoints through Oak.

Thanks to the Oak team for a smooth integration. More to come. 

https://t.co/AB3lURs1fq

Upoch is now officially integrated with @OakAgentKit.

As of Oak 0.3.0, any AI agent running on Oak can query Upoch directly. Ask about a workflow and the agent gets its roles, checkpoint history, past recoveries and Upoch Score. It can also browse workflows ranked by score, without leaving the conversation.

All of it is read directly from the Upoch contract on Robinhood Chain, and every workflow's metadata passes Oak's Agent Wormhole safety check before an agent sees it.

This first release is read-only. The next step, which we're building together with the Oak team, is letting agents register workflows and submit checkpoints through Oak.

https://t.co/AB3lURs1fq
full_text_zh:
Upoch 现已与 @OakAgentKit 正式集成。

从 Oak 0.3.0 开始，任何在 Oak 上运行的 AI 代理都可以直接查询 Upoch。询问工作流程，代理会获取其角色、检查点历史记录、过去的恢复情况和 Upoch 分数。它还可以浏览按分数排名的工作流程，而无需离开对话。

所有这些都是直接从 Robinhood Chain 上的 Upoch 合约读取的，每个工作流程的元数据在代理看到之前都通过了 Oak 的 Agent Wormhole 安全检查。

第一个版本是只读的。我们与 Oak 团队共同构建的下一步是让代理通过 Oak 注册工作流程并提交检查点。

感谢Oak团队的顺利整合。未来还会有更多。

title_en:
What happens when someone sells a @meetmotes NFT with an active AI agent?

This is an important detail people shouldn't overlook.

Motes proposed transfer process checks outstanding balances, debt and open positions, revokes active agent permissions and settles financial commitments before ownership changes.

I believe this is necessary. Nobody should buy an NFT only to discover unexpected financial obligations attached to it.

Digital ownership should come with financial clarity.

我相信这是必要

title:
I've changed how I work over the last few weeks.

I now have one lead agent for each area of focus, running all the time
title_en:
I've changed how I work over the last few weeks.

I now have one lead agent for each area of focus, running all the time, and a chief of staff agent that oversees them. Each lead manages its own sub-agents that write code, test it, chase reviews, and coordinate with team members.

Everything I need to decide or review comes into one prioritized queue, a simple local web app. Each product review includes screenshots and a video demo of the feature. I clear the queue in batches, mostly by voice and keyboard shortcuts. The leads also bring back ideas I hadn't considered.

Working from one queue, instead of switching between dozens of chats, has cut a lot of mental overhead. The system keeps learning my preferences and distilling my judgment into a "Brian brain," so its recommendations and first drafts get better before they reach me. The goal is fewer corrections per change.

Every change still goes through the same human review and security checks. It is eliminating tasks, not human judgment.

What an exciting time to push the frontier of productivity, especially as we build the economy for agents (agentic finance). We should all keep pushing in this direction.
title_zh:
过去几周我改变了工作方式。

我现在每个重点领域都有一名首席代理人，一直在运行，还有一名幕僚长代理人负责监督他们。每个领导管理自己的子代理，负责编写代码、测试代码、追踪评论并与团队成员协调。

我需要决定或审查的所有内容都会进入一个优先队列

full_text_zh:
过去几周我改变了工作方式。

我现在每个重点领域都有一名首席代理人，一直在运行，还有一名幕僚长代理人负责监督他们。每个领导管理自己的子代理，负责编写代码、测试代码、追踪评论并与团队成员协调。

我需要决定或审查的所有内容都会进入一个优先队列，一个简单的本地网络应用程序。每个产品评论都包含该功能的屏幕截图和视频演示。我主要通过语音和键盘快捷键批量清除队列。这些线索也带回了我没有考虑过的想法。

在一个队列中工作，而不是在数十个聊天之间切换，已经减少了很多精神负担。该系统不断学习我的偏好，并将我的判断提炼到“布莱恩大脑”中，因此它的建议和初稿在到达我手中之前会变得更好。目标是减少每次更改的纠正次数。

每项更改仍然要经过相同的人工审查和安全检查。它消除的是任务，而不是人的判断。

这是推动生产力前沿的激动人心的时刻，尤其是当我们为代理（代理金融）建立经济时。我们都应该继续朝这个方向努力。

title_en:
This is the part of AI agent infrastructure I actually care about.

Not a smarter model. An approve button. An agent wants to run a migration, I'm not at my desk, and I get to say yes or no from my phone before anything happens.

I'm bullish on agents, but control has to come before trust. Tools that make it easy to supervise, pause, or kill a run are what will let people hand agents real responsibility. https://t.co/RoCHThamGw

this time, i decided
title_en:
i’ve been exploring @MojoAI_HQ and getting familiar with how different parts of the platform work.

this time, i decided to focus on market monitoring and see how Mojo AI Agent could help me keep up with market movements without constantly checking charts myself.

i tried a couple of prompts:

→ 𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗻

“𝗰𝗿𝗲𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗮 𝗦𝗢𝗟 𝘁𝗿𝗮𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗽𝗹𝗮𝗻 𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝟰-𝗵𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲𝗳𝗿𝗮𝗺𝗲. 𝗶𝗻𝗰𝗹𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗿𝘆, 𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗽 𝗹𝗼𝘀𝘀, 𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗳𝗶𝘁, 𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗸-𝘁𝗼-𝗿𝗲𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗱 𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗶𝗻𝘃𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗹𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗹.”

→ 𝗺𝗼𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗲𝘁

“𝗺𝗼𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗼𝗿 𝗦𝗢𝗟 𝗳𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗱 𝗽𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗲 𝗺𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀. 𝗮𝗹𝗲𝗿𝘁 𝗺𝗲 𝘄𝗵𝗲𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗮 𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗻𝗶𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗻𝘁 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲.”

the idea was to see how easily I could get market insights, create a trading plan and monitor potential opportunities using simple instructions.

i haven’t executed any trades yet.
this was purely about exploring the monitoring and analysis side of Mojo.

i also put together a quick walkthrough showing how to get started, navigate the platform and use its features.

what’s interesting is how you can communicate your trading ideas in plain English without having to figure everything out manually.

im still exploring, still learning
more Mojo experiments coming.

#Mojo

title:

A creator reportedly used Claude Code to investigate his Andro
title_en:
🚨 YOUR ANDROID PHONE MAY BE STORING MORE THAN YOU THINK.

A creator reportedly used Claude Code to investigate his Android device and discovered over 14,219 images in hidden system directories.

The shocking part? Some appeared to be captured by the front camera.

Here’s what he reportedly found:

→ Images stored outside the normal gallery
→ Face Unlock and system-related cache files
→ Thousands of regular and infrared images
→ Files potentially containing timestamps and location metadata

How did he uncover them?

He connected his Android phone to a computer and used Claude Code to investigate hidden directories.

The discovery raises serious questions about how facial recognition systems process and store biometric data.

⚠️ Important: Hidden image files don’t automatically mean someone is spying on you. Some may be temporary facial recognition data, diagnostic files, or cached images. This claim also hasn’t been independently verified.

Still, it’s a reminder to review your camera permissions, privacy settings, and device storage.

AI isn’t just helping us build things anymore.

It’s helping us investigate what our devices might be hiding.

Would you trust your phone’s facial recognition after seeing this? 👀

Save this post for your next Android privacy check.

full_text_zh:
🚨 您的 Android 手机存储的数据可能比您想象的还要多。

据报道，一名创作者使用 Claude Code 来调查他的 Android 设备，并在隐藏的系统目录中发现了超过 14,219 张图像。

令人震惊的部分？有些似乎是由前置摄像头捕捉到的。

据报道，这是他的发现：

→ 存储在普通图库之外的图像
→ 人脸解锁和系统相关的缓存文件
→ 数千张常规图像和红外图像
→ 可能包含时间戳和位置元数据的文件

他是如何发现它们的？

他将 Android 手机连接到计算机，并使用 Claude Code 来调查隐藏目录。

这一发现引发了关于面部识别系统如何处理和存储生物识别数据的严重问题。

⚠️重要提示：隐藏图像文件并不自动意味着有人在监视您。有些可能是临时面部识别数据、诊断文件或缓存图像。这一说法也尚未得到独立证实。

尽管如此，还是提醒您检查您的相机权限、隐私设置和设备存储。

人工智能不再只是帮助我们建造东西。

它帮助我们调查我们的设备可能隐藏了什么。

Great paper from Google on making ML experiments reproducible for coding agents.

(bookmark it)

If you run agents on research code, this one is worth your time.

They find that refined artifacts raise agent reproduction success from 76.4% to 92.6% across four models and cut API spending by 19.7%.

ReproBridge turns one successful reproduction into a package the next agent can reuse. The package holds the cleaned code, the environment setup, scripts that launch each experiment, and a written guide.

A new agent reruns the experiment from that package. A separate auditor then checks that the runs actually happened.

The benchmark covers 1,029 tasks from 36 papers, each with five human-verified reference scores. The gap between the best and worst model drops from 21.6 to 3.9 points. Removing the code or the environment setup causes the largest losses.

If your agents keep failing to rerun a repo, save the setup steps from the first successful run before trying a bigger model.

title_en:
𝗖𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲 𝗖𝗼𝗱𝗲 𝘁𝗶𝗽: the $20 plan now runs your whole session on Opus 5.5 by default. To make your quota last longer, switch the main session to Sonnet 5.5 and keep Opus on call with /advisor.

Launch with claude --model sonnet --advisor opus to make Opus 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝗱𝘃𝗶𝘀𝗼𝗿 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝘀𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀. Sonnet 5.5 keeps doing the work and calls Opus in at three moments:
→ Before committing to a plan: is it right?
→ When the same error keeps coming back: am I heading the wrong way?
→ Before saying "done": did I miss anything?
Opus reads the whole session and gives advice. Sonnet still writes the code.

Hand the tree and this prompt to Claude Code to set it up 👇

"Set up my Claude Code to match this tree:
1. For the three subagents in the tree, check ~/.claude/agents and .claude/agents first. Reuse fitting ones, and propose new ones only for missing roles. Set the ones that read code and look up docs to model: haiku, and the one that edits code and runs tests to model: sonnet. Leave any subagent that already sets a different model alone, and list it.
2. In ~/.claude/settings.json, set model to sonnet and advisorModel to opus.
3. Check these environment variables and report them without changing anything: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL turns the advisor off, and so does DISABLE_TELEMETRY or anything else that stops flag fetching. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE forces every subagent onto one model. Then check the version: if Claude Code is older than 2.1.293, tell me (in earlier versions, haiku still meant Haiku 4.5). Don't upgrade it yourself.
4. Add one rule to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md: ask the advisor before committing to a big plan, when the same error shows up a second time, and before calling a long task done.

Show me the changes first. Don't edit any files yet."

title: Replit was building toward the AI coding era years before it had a name. In 2024, the company shipped an agent that coul
title_en:
Replit was building toward the AI coding era years before it had a name. In 2024, the company shipped an agent that could take a request in plain English, work through errors, provision its own infrastructure, and keep going until the software actually worked. The model companies even reached out to ask how Replit had pulled it off.

Co-founder and CEO Amjad Masad had been thinking about making programming radically more accessible since 2008, and Replit’s original pitch deck predicted AI-generated code before the Transformer paper was published. Today, that same technology is moving into banks, manufacturers, and other large companies, where Amjad says teams are replacing software projects once scoped at $10 million with $250,000 of Replit.

On How to Build the Future, @paulg sits down with @amasad to talk about why @Replit was so well positioned when coding agents arrived, what comes after vibe coding, and his bigger vision for the “self-driving company,” where AI agents increasingly build and operate the software a company needs.

title:
holy f*ck... the best AI agents don't have a better model. they have better notes

Stanford University just published th
title_en:
holy f*ck... the best AI agents don't have a better model. they have better notes

Stanford University just published the whole method for free in a paper called Agentic Context Engineering. your agent reviews every run, writes down each lesson and adds it to its notes. it never rewrites them, so nothing it learns is ever lost

same weights, zero fine-tuning. 38.6% → 64.2%, level with IBM's top production agent on Opus 5.5. fine-tuning for that jump costs $5,000-20,000. here it cost $0

it comes down to 4 agents:

→ worker: does the task and saves the full log
→ critic: reads the log and marks every mistake and every win
→ teacher: turns each one into a one-line lesson
→ librarian: files the lesson into CLAUDE.md. merges duplicates, never deletes a line

that's why asking your agent to "clean up" your CLAUDE.md is a mistake. every rewrite throws away lessons it already paid for

paste this into Claude Code:

"Run 4 agents on my last 10 sessions in ~/.claude/projects. Critic: mark every mistake and every win. Teacher: turn each one into a one-line lesson, what happened and what to do next time. Librarian: add only new lessons to my CLAUDE.md under ## Lessons, merge exact duplicates, never rewrite or delete an existing line. Worker: rerun 2 of the failed tasks with the new lessons and save the full log. Show me the diff and both results before saving"

run it after every big session. your agent gets smarter every time and it costs $0

full playbook below ↓

full_text_zh:
天啊……最好的人工智能代理没有更好的模型。他们有更好的笔记

斯坦福大学刚刚在一篇名为 Agentic Context Engineering 的论文中免费发布了整个方法。您的代理会审查每次跑步，写下每节课并将其添加到笔记中。它从不重写它们，所以它学到的任何东西都不会丢失

相同的权重，零微调。 38.6% → 64.2%，与 Opus 5.5 上 IBM 顶级生产代理持平。微调这一跳跃的成本为 5,000-20,000 美元。这里花费 0 美元

归结为 4 个代理：

→worker：执行任务并保存完整日志
→ 评论家：阅读日志并标记每个错误和每次胜利
→ 老师：将每一课变成一行课
→ 图书管理员：将课程归档到 CLAUDE.md 中。合并重复项，从不删除行

这就是为什么要求您的代理“清理”您的 CLAUDE.md 是一个错误。每次重写都会丢掉已经付出代价的教训

将其粘贴到 Claude Code 中：

“在 ~/.claude/projects 中的最后 10 个会话中运行 4 个代理。评论家：标记每个错误和每次胜利。教师：将每个错误变成单行课程，说明发生了什么以及下次要做什么。图书管理员：仅将新课程添加到 ## Lessons 下的 CLAUDE.md 中，合并精确的重复项，切勿重写或删除现有行。工作人员：使用新课程重新运行 2 个失败的任务，并保存完整日志。显示差异和两者保存前的结果”

每次大型会议后运行它。您的代理每次都会变得更聪明，而且成本为 0 美元

title_en:
$PLTR Palantir Stock Investors Just Got Great News From a Wall Street Analyst 
(Hint: The Stock Could Soar) 🚀📈🔮
JPMorgan Chase analyst Brian Essex believes Palantir is deeply undervalued: “Palantir’s strategy is to build and offer a platform that can accommodate the world’s most difficult and highest-return AI use cases.” 🎯👊🏻💥

Nov 7, 2026
Key Points
🔹JPMorgan Chase analyst Brian Essex recently initiated coverage of Palantir; his target price of $262 per share is one of the highest on Wall Street.

🔹Palantir is a leader in artificial intelligence platforms, and its ontology-based software arguably gives it a durable competitive advantage.

🔹Palantir is the most expensive stock in the S&P 500 in terms of its price-to-sales ratio, but Essex says the valuation is justified by rapid revenue growth.

Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ: PLTR) has been one of the biggest winners of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, in both share price appreciation and business expansion. The stock has added 2,400% since ChatGPT popularized generative AI in January 2023, and revenue growth has accelerated in 13 consecutive quarters.

Palantir investors recently got great news. In late October, JPMorgan Chase analyst Brian Essex initiated coverage of the company, awarding Palantir a buy rating and a target price of $262 per share. That is one of the most bullish forecasts on Wall Street and it implies 63% upside from the current share price of $160. 🚀

Here’s what investors need to know.

Palantir is a recognized leader in artificial intelligence platforms ✔️

Palantir develops analytics platforms that help government and commercial customers integrate and make sense of complex data. The company supplements its core analytics products with an integrated artificial intelligence (AI) platform called AIP, which serves as a large language model orchestration tool that lets clients swap models without rewriting applications, while retaining control over their sensitive data.

Brian Essex at JPMorgan Chase argues that Palantir has a durable economic moat in its ontology-based software. An ontology unifies data from disparate systems into critical workflows, helping clients make better decisions and automate business processes. For example, Palantir can help manufacturers navigate supplier delays by identifying which customer orders are at risk and deciding how to reallocate inventory.

Forrester Research recently recognized Palantir as a leader in AI platforms. In terms of current capabilities, the analysts ranked its platform above products from all competitors except C3. ai, but the report distinguished Palantir as having the stronger growth strategy. “Palantir’s strategy is to build and offer a platform that can accommodate the world’s most difficult and highest-return AI use cases.” 🔥

Palantir’s revenue growth has now accelerated in 13 straight quarters

JPMorgan Chase analyst Brian Essex justified his target price in a recent note. “As we move from a year where enterprises are just figuring out how to deploy the most transformational technology we have seen in our lifetime to one where they are looking for return, Palantir is already delivering ROI by leveraging its platform to fundamentally transform the business operations of its customers, and growth is accelerating.” 👊🏻

Indeed, Palantir has consistently delivered impressive financial results. In the third quarter, revenue increased 96% to $2.3 billion, marking the 13th straight acceleration. That strong top-line growth was driven largely by momentum in the U.S. commercial business, where sales increased 119%. Meanwhile, non-GAAP earnings soared 144% to $0.44 per diluted share.

In his shareholder letter, CEO Alex Karp wrote, “We have now essentially doubled our entire business since the same quarter last year.” And he expects that strength to persist for the foreseeable future. Palantir raised its full-year guidance, with sales now forecast to climb 156% to $8.5 billion in 2026, a significant acceleration from the 75% sales growth reported in 2025. 🦄

JPMorgan’s Brian Essex is not concerned by Palantir’s expensive valuation 🎯

For many investors, Palantir’s rich valuation punches a hole in the investment thesis. Yes, the company has emerged as the standard in enterprise AI, and its business is growing at a phenomenal pace. But the current valuation of 53 times sales makes it the most expensive stock in the S&P 500, with Moderna ranking second at 47 times sales.

Is the business growing quickly enough to justify that valuation multiple? Brian Essex at JPMorgan says the answer is yes. “Valuation is reasonable when taking into account the company’s uniquely profitable hyper-growth fundamentals, with potential for substantial disruptive upside within its primary market segments,” he wrote in a note to clients.

Many Wall Street analysts agree with Essex and think the stock is undervalued at its current price. In fact, among 38 analysts who follow the company, Palantir has a median target price of $235 per share. That implies 46% upside from the current share price of $160.
By Trevor Jennewine, The Motley Fool

Palantir 开发的分析平台可帮助政府和商业客户集成并理解复杂的数据。该公司通过名为 AIP 的集成人工智能 (AI) 平台对其核心分析产品进行了补充，该平台作为大型语言模型编排工具，允许客户在不重写应用程序的情况下交换模型，同时保留对其敏感数据的控制。

摩根大通的布莱恩·埃塞克斯 (Brian Essex) 认为，Palantir 在其基于本体的软件中拥有持久的经济护城河。本体将来自不同系统的数据统一到关键工作流程中，帮助客户做出更好的决策并实现业务流程自动化。例如，Palantir 可以通过识别哪些客户订单存在风险并决定如何重新分配库存来帮助制造商解决供应商延误问题。

Forrester Research 最近将 Palantir 认定为人工智能平台的领导者。就目前的功能而言，分析师将其平台排在除 C3 之外的所有竞争对手的产品之上。 ai，但该报告指出 Palantir 拥有更强大的增长战略。 “Palantir 的战略是构建并提供一个能够适应世界上最困难和回报最高的人工智能用例的平台。” 🔥

Palantir 的收入增长现已连续 13 个季度加速

摩根大通分析师布莱恩·埃塞克斯在最近的一份报告中证明了他的目标价是合理的。 “当我们从企业刚刚弄清楚如何部署我们一生中见过的最具变革性的技术的一年转向寻求回报的一年时，Palantir 已经通过利用其平台从根本上改变客户的业务运营来提供投资回报，并且增长正在加速。” 👊🏻

事实上，Palantir 一直取得令人印象深刻的财务业绩。第三季度收入增长 96%，达到 23 亿美元，连续第 13 个季度增长。收入的强劲增长主要是由美国商业业务的势头推动的，该业务的销售额增长了 119%。与此同时，非 GAAP 收益飙升 144% 至稀释后每股 0.44 美元。

首席执行官亚历克斯·卡普（Alex Karp）在致股东的信中写道：“自去年同一季度以来，我们的整体业务基本上翻了一番。”他预计这种力量在可预见的未来将持续存在。 Palantir 上调了全年指引，目前预计 2026 年销售额将增长 156%，达到 85 亿美元，比 2025 年报告的 75% 销售额增长显着加速。🦄

摩根大通的 Brian Essex 并不担心 Palantir 昂贵的估值 🎯

对于许多投资者来说，Palantir 的高估值在投资论点上留下了漏洞。是的，该公司已经成为企业人工智能的标准，并且其业务正在以惊人的速度增长。但目前53倍销售额的估值使其成为标准普尔500指数中最昂贵的股票，Moderna以47倍销售额排名第二。

该业务的增长速度是否足以证明该估值倍数是合理的？摩根大通的布莱恩·埃塞克斯 (Brian Essex) 表示答案是肯定的。他在给客户的一份报告中写道：“考虑到该公司独特的盈利高速增长基本面，以及在其主要细分市场内具有巨大颠覆性上涨潜力的潜力，估值是合理的。”

许多华尔街分析师同意埃塞克斯的观点，认为该股目前的价格被低估。事实上，在关注该公司的 38 名分析师中，Palantir 的目标价中位数为每股 235 美元。这意味着较当前 160 美元的股价上涨 46%。
